Distance to a reference location

Source: R/spatial_distance.R
step_spatial_distance.Rd

step_spatial_distance() creates a specification of a recipe step that will compute the distance from each point in one or more geometry columns to a reference: a fixed set of points (ref), or a second geometry column in the data (ref_col).

Usage

step_spatial_distance(
  recipe,
  ...,
  ref = NULL,
  ref_col = NULL,
  metric = c("haversine", "euclidean", "manhattan"),
  role = "predictor",
  trained = FALSE,
  columns = NULL,
  crs = NULL,
  keep_original_cols = FALSE,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = rand_id("spatial_distance")
)

Arguments

recipe

A recipe object. The step will be added to the sequence of operations for this recipe.

...

One or more selector functions to choose which geometry columns (sfc columns of points) to compute distances from, for example all_geometry_predictors(). See recipes::selections() for more details.

ref

An sfc or sf object of points to measure distances to. It is evaluated when the step is created and stored in the step. It is transformed to the CRS of each selected column when the recipe is trained. Exactly one of ref and ref_col must be given.

ref_col

Bare name of a second geometry column in the data to measure distances to, row by row. It must select exactly one sfc column with the same CRS as the columns in ..., and is never itself used as a column to measure from. Exactly one of ref and ref_col must be given.

metric

A single string, one of "haversine", "euclidean" or "manhattan". "haversine" measures great-circle distance on a sphere with a radius of 6371008.8 meters, requires longitude and latitude coordinates, and returns meters. "euclidean" and "manhattan" measure in the units of a projected (or missing) CRS and error on longitude and latitude coordinates. Defaults to "haversine".

role

Not used by this step since no new variables are created.

trained

A logical to indicate if the quantities for preprocessing have been estimated.

columns

A character string of the selected variable names. This field is a placeholder and will be populated once recipes::prep() is used.

crs

A named list of the CRS of each geometry column, recorded when recipes::prep() is used. This field is a placeholder and is not meant to be set by the user.

keep_original_cols

A logical to keep the original geometry columns after the distances are computed. Defaults to FALSE.

skip

A logical. Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by bake()? While all operations are baked when prep() is run, some operations may not be able to be conducted on new data (e.g. processing the outcome variable(s)). Care should be taken when using skip = TRUE as it may affect the computations for subsequent operations.

id

A character string that is unique to this step to identify it.

Value

An updated version of recipe with the new step added to the sequence of existing steps (if any).

Details

Only point geometries are supported. Rows with an empty point (such as the ones step_sfc_point() creates for missing coordinates) get a distance of NA.

The new columns are plain numeric vectors, not units objects, and depend on what is passed to the step:

  • With ref, every selected column gets one new column for each point in ref, named {column}_dist_{i} where i is the position of the point in ref. One reference point gives one column and five reference points give five, each holding the distance from that row to that point. The distances to all points are computed for every row.

  • With ref_col, every selected column gets a single new column named {column}_dist. The distance is computed row by row, between the point in the selected column and the point in ref_col on the same row.

The CRS of the geometry columns is recorded in recipes::prep(), and recipes::bake() errors if the CRS of the new data differs.

Tidying

When you tidy() this step, a tibble is returned with columns terms, metric, and id:

terms

character, the selectors or variables selected

metric

character, the distance metric

id

character, id of this step

Examples

library(recipes)
data(ames, package = "modeldata")

# Hand-picked points: the Iowa State University Campanile and the Ames Main
# Street Historic District
fixed_points <- sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_point(c(-93.6460, 42.0254)),
  sf::st_point(c(-93.6136, 42.0256)),
  crs = 4326
)

rec <- recipe(Sale_Price ~ Longitude + Latitude, data = ames) |>
  step_sfc_point(lon = Longitude, lat = Latitude) |>
  step_spatial_distance(all_geometry_predictors(), ref = fixed_points) |>
  prep()

# One column per reference point
bake(rec, new_data = NULL)
#> # A tibble: 2,930 × 3
#>    Sale_Price geometry_dist_1 geometry_dist_2
#>         <int>           <dbl>           <dbl>
#>  1     215000           3852.           3202.
#>  2     105000           3758.           3090.
#>  3     172000           3744.           3047.
#>  4     244000           3724.           2868.
#>  5     189900           3990.           4448.
#>  6     195500           3977.           4436.
#>  7     213500           4298.           4478.
#>  8     191500           4055.           4248.
#>  9     236500           4118.           4258.
#> 10     189000           3801.           4287.
#> # ℹ 2,920 more rows

tidy(rec, number = 2)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   terms    metric    id                    
#>   <chr>    <chr>     <chr>                 
#> 1 geometry haversine spatial_distance_lYqjR
